title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram

concept.title: For every bar: how far can it stretch to the left and to the right?
body: A histogram has bars of width 1. The largest rectangle inside it has a **bar as its lowest bar** (otherwise it could be made taller). So for every bar `h[i]` we want the widest range around `i` in which all bars are at least `h[i]` high: the rectangle has the area `h[i] * width`. The range ends at the nearest **smaller** bar on each side.

Both nearest smaller bars come from one pass with a **stack of indexes whose heights are increasing**. When a new bar `h[i]` is lower than or equal to the bar on top, the top bar cannot stretch further to the right: its right end is `i`. After popping it, the bar below it on the stack is the nearest smaller bar on its left. So at the moment of a pop we know both ends.

body.code:
best = 0; stack = []
for i in range(n + 1):
    cur = h[i] if i < n else 0          # a bar of height 0 at the end empties the stack
    while stack and h[stack[-1]] >= cur:
        height = h[stack.pop()]
        left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
        best = max(best, height * (i - left - 1))
    stack.append(i)

body: The width is `i - left - 1`: the bars strictly between the two nearest smaller bars. Every index is pushed and popped once, so the time is O(n). The area can be large (`20000 * 10^9`), so use 64-bit integers in C++ and Java.

statement: A histogram has `n` bars, each of width 1, and the heights are given from left to right. Print the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the histogram (the rectangle covers consecutive bars).

examples.note: The bars 5 and 6 (height 5, width 2) give the area 10.

hints: In the best rectangle, the lowest bar touches the top edge. Try every bar as the lowest one.
For a bar you need the nearest smaller bar on the left and on the right.
Keep a stack of bars with increasing heights; when a lower bar arrives, pop and measure.

explanation: A stack keeps the indexes of bars with increasing heights. A lower bar pops the higher bars; at each pop the nearest smaller bars on both sides are known, so the widest rectangle of the popped bar is measured.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
h = list(map(int, input().split()))

best = 0
stack = []
for i in range(n + 1):
    cur = h[i] if i < n else 0
    while stack and h[stack[-1]] >= cur:
        height = h[stack.pop()]
        left = stack[-1] if stack else -1
        best = max(best, height * (i - left - 1))
    stack.append(i)
print(best)
